zajjaj:21-21.t: His words: ﴿وَلا تَكُونُوا كالَّذِينَ قالُوا سَمِعْنا وهم لا يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ — by this are meant those who said: ﴿قَدْ سَمِعْنا لَوْ نَشاءُ لَقُلْنا مِثْلَ هَذا﴾ [al-Anfāl: 31]. Allah — glorious is His praise — called them "لا يَسْمَعُونَ" (they do not hear) because they listened with the listening of enmity and hatred; they did not try to understand and did not reflect, so they were in the position of one who has not heard.

zajjaj:22-22.t: His words: ﴿إنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الصُّمُّ البُكْمُ﴾ — by this are meant those who hear and understand, yet in their refusal to accept are in the position of one who has neither heard nor comprehended.

zajjaj:23-23.t: ﴿وَلَوْ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا لأسْمَعَهُمْ﴾, that is: had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear the answer to everything they ask about. Then He — Mighty and Majestic — said: ﴿وَلَوْ أسْمَعَهم لَتَوَلَّوْا وهم مُعْرِضُونَ﴾, that is: had He made clear to them everything that stirs in their souls, they would still have turned away, averse, because of their obstinacy.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
His words: ﴿اسْتَجِيبُوا لِلَّهِ ولِلرَّسُولِ إذا دَعاكم لِما يُحْيِيكُمْ﴾, that is: to that which is a cause of life, namely knowledge. It is also possible that it means: to that which is a cause of everlasting life in the bliss of the Hereafter. The meaning of "اِسْتَجِيبُوا" is that of "أجِيبُوا" (respond). The poet said:
وَداعٍ دَعا يا مَن يُجِيبُ إلى النِّدا ∗∗∗ فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِبْهُ عِنْدَ ذاكَ مُجِيبُ
(A caller called out, "O who will answer the call?" — but at that moment no answerer responded to him.)
that is: no one answered him.
His words: ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ المَرْءِ وقَلْبِهِ﴾ — three views have been stated about it. Some said: "He comes between the believer and disbelief," and "He comes between the disbeliever and faith by death," that is: "He comes between a person and what he keeps postponing for himself, by death." It was also said: "يَحُولُ بَيْنَ المَرْءِ وقَلْبِهِ" means: "Know that Allah is with a person in nearness to this degree," as He — Mighty and Majestic — said: ﴿وَنَحْنُ أقْرَبُ إلَيْهِ مِن حَبْلِ الوَرِيدِ﴾ [Qāf: 16]. And it was said: they used to think about the great number of their enemy and their own small number, so fear entered their hearts; so Allah — glorious is His praise — made known that He comes between a man and his heart, by replacing his fear with security, and giving their enemy — in place of their supposing that they had the power over them — cowardice and weakness.

zajjaj:25-25.t: ﴿واتَّقُوا فِتْنَةً لا تُصِيبَنَّ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنكم خاصَّةً﴾, that is: beware lest the wrongdoers be repaid with a vengeance from Allah. By this are meant the rebellious ringleaders of the hypocrites who used to bar people from faith in Allah. Some grammarians claimed that the speech is a conditional apodosis (jazāʾ) containing an element of prohibition. So when you say: "اِنْزِلْ عَنِ الدّابَّةِ لا تَطْرَحْكَ، ولا تَطْرَحَنَّكَ" (get down from the riding beast, it will not throw you / let it not throw you), this is the answer to the command in the wording of a prohibition, and the meaning is: "If you get down from it, it will not throw you." When you add the light or the heavy nūn, it makes the speech more emphatic. Similar to it is: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَساكِنَكُمْ﴾ [al-Naml: 18]: she commanded them to enter, then forbade them from being crushed by Sulaymān, saying: "لا يَحْطِمَنَّكم سُلَيْمانُ وجُنُودُهُ" — the wording of the prohibition is addressed to Sulaymān, but its meaning is for the ants; just as you say: "لا أرَيَنَّكَ هَهُنا" (let me not see you here): the wording of the prohibition is directed at yourself, but its meaning is: "Do not be here, for I will see you."

zajjaj:30-30.t: His words: ﴿وَإذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ﴾ — the meaning is: "And remember when those who disbelieved were plotting against you." Allah — glorious is His praise — reminded him of a favour He had bestowed on him: the help and victory on the day of Badr — that is what is meant — and He said: "وَإذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا", that is: "Remember those circumstances." ﴿وَيَمْكُرُونَ ويَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ واللَّهُ خَيْرُ الماكِرِينَ﴾ — because Allah's plotting is only requital and help for the believers; hence Allah is the best of planners.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
﴿وَإذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا قالُوا قَدْ سَمِعْنا لَوْ نَشاءُ لَقُلْنا مِثْلَ هَذا إنْ هَذا إلا أساطِيرُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ — yet they had been challenged to bring a single sūra like the Qur'an, and they did not bring it.
His words: ﴿إنْ هَذا إلا أساطِيرُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ — its singular is "أُسْطُورَةٌ"; they mean the lies that the ancients wrote down. Then they said: ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ مِن عِنْدِكَ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32]. The reading is with "اَلْحَقَّ" in the accusative (naṣb), as the khabar (predicate) of "كانَ", and "هو" was brought in as a separating pronoun (faṣl); we have explained this earlier in the book. Know that "هو" has no grammatical position in our view, and that it is like the emphasising "ما"; it was brought in so that it would be known that "اَلْحَقَّ" is not an adjective of "هَذا", but rather that it is the khabar. "هو الحَقُّ مِن عِنْدِكَ" (with the nominative) is permissible, but I know of no one who read it so, though there is no disagreement among the grammarians that it is allowable; but reading is a sunna (an established practice), in which one reads only according to a transmitted reading.
His words: ﴿فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ أوِ ائْتِنا بِعَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32] — the meaning is: "And remember when they said this." They said it by way of rejecting it, and they said it while the Prophet ﷺ was among them. So Allah made known that He would not punish them while His Messenger was among them, and said: ﴿وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهم وأنْتَ فِيهِمْ وما كانَ اللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهم وهم يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 33], that is: "Allah would not punish them while among them are those whose affair will end in Islam." He said: ﴿وَما لَهم ألا يُعَذِّبَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 34] — the meaning is: what is there for them in the leaving-off of the punishment?! — that is: its being warded off from them — ﴿وَهم يَصُدُّونَ عَنِ المَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ وما كانُوا أوْلِياءَهُ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 34]; the meaning is: "while they bar its guardians from the Sacred Mosque, and they were not its guardians." ﴿إنْ أوْلِياؤُهُ إلا المُتَّقُونَ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 34] — the meaning is: "Its guardians are none but the God-fearing." So Allah made known to the Prophet ﷺ that He would not punish them with the punishment that befell them — killing and captivity — while he was among them, nor inflict that punishment on those of them whose affair would end in Islam; and He made known to him that He would not ward off from the whole of them the punishment He inflicted on them. Then He made known that, with their barring, they were not the guardians of the Sacred Mosque nor the friends of Allah; their way of drawing near to Allah — Mighty and Majestic — was only whistling and clapping. So He — Mighty and Majestic — said: ﴿وَما كانَ صَلاتُهم عِنْدَ البَيْتِ إلا مُكاءً وتَصْدِيَةً﴾ [al-Anfāl: 35]. المُكاءُ is whistling, and التَّصْدِيَةُ is clapping.

zajjaj:37-37.t: His words: ﴿لِيَمِيزَ اللَّهُ الخَبِيثَ مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ﴾, that is: so that He may distinguish what the believers spent in obedience to Allah from what the idolaters spent in disobedience to Allah. ﴿وَيَجْعَلَ الخَبِيثَ بَعْضَهُ عَلى بَعْضٍ فَيَرْكُمَهُ جَمِيعًا﴾ — "اَلرَّكْمُ" is to place part of a thing upon another part. One says: "رَكَمْتُ الشَّيْءَ، أرْكُمُهُ، رَكْمًا" (I heaped the thing up), and "اَلرُّكامُ" is the noun. ﴿فَيَجْعَلَهُ في جَهَنَّمَ﴾, that is: He places part of what the idolaters spent upon another part, and it is placed upon them in the Fire, so it becomes part of that with which they are punished, as He — Mighty and Majestic — said: ﴿فَتُكْوى بِها جِباهُهم وجُنُوبُهم وظُهُورُهُمْ﴾ [al-Tawba: 35].

zajjaj:39-39.t: His words: ﴿وَقاتِلُوهم حَتّى لا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾, that is: until people are no longer tempted with the temptation (fitna) of disbelief. What indicates the meaning "temptation of disbelief" is His words — Mighty and Majestic —: ﴿وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ كُلُّهُ لِلَّهِ﴾.

zajjaj:40-40.t: His words: ﴿وَإنْ تَوَلَّوْا فاعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلاكُمْ﴾ — the meaning is: "If they persist in their disbelief and enmity, then know that Allah is your mawlā (protector)," that is: "He is the protector for you," so their hostility will not harm you.

zajjaj:41-41.t:
His words: ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّما غَنِمْتُمْ مِن شَيْءٍ فَأنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ ولِلرَّسُولِ ولِذِي القُرْبى واليَتامى والمَساكِينِ وابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ — people have disagreed a great deal about the interpretation of this verse and about acting upon it. In sum, it concerns one of the kinds of wealth in which Allah — glorious is His praise — has laid down obligatory shares. The kinds of wealth in which mention is made of obligatory shares for the poor, the needy and those like them are three, and Allah named each kind. He named the wealth that the Muslims take from the idolaters in a state of war "anfāl" and "ghanāʾim" (spoils); what came to the Muslims without being taken in war — such as the kharāj (land tax) and the jizya (poll tax) — was named "fayʾ"; and what goes out of the wealth of the Muslims — such as zakāt, the vows they have vowed, and that by which they seek nearness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic — was named "ṣadaqa" (alms). This is the sum of the naming of the kinds of wealth. In this verse we will set out what the majority of jurists have said and what the language requires, if Allah wills.
Abū Isḥāq said: The jurists are agreed that four-fifths of the spoils belong exclusively to the combatants, while the fifth that is named in His words ﴿فَأنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ ولِلرَّسُولِ﴾, to the end of the verse, is subject to disagreement. As for al-Shāfiʿī, he stated that this fifth is divided among those whom Allah — Mighty and Majestic — named as entitled to its division, and he made His words ﴿فَأنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ﴾ an opening of speech. Abū Isḥāq said: I reckon that the meaning of "an opening of speech" in his view here is that all things belong to Allah — Mighty and Majestic — so He began and opened the speech.
So if someone says: "فَأنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ", it is as He said: ﴿يَسْألُونَكَ عَنِ الأنْفالِ قُلِ الأنْفالُ لِلَّهِ والرَّسُولِ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 1]. Then he divided this fifth into five portions: a fifth for the Prophet ﷺ, a fifth for the orphans of the Muslims — not for the orphans of the Prophet's family ﷺ — a fifth for the needy — the needy of the Muslims, not the needy of the Prophet ﷺ — and a fifth for the wayfarer. «[Translator's note: only four of the five portions are listed in the text as transmitted; the portion of the near kin (ذوو القربى) is not mentioned here.]» Al-Shāfiʿī does not hold that any one of these categories may be left without a share in the division. Abū Isḥāq said: It has reached me that he holds that some of them may be favoured over others according to need, and he holds, regarding the share of the Messenger ﷺ, that it is spent on what the Prophet ﷺ used to spend it on. What is transmitted is that he used to spend the fifth on equipment for the Muslims, such as acquiring weapons by which their strength would be increased. This is the school of al-Shāfiʿī, and it follows the wording of what is in the Book.
As for Abū Ḥanīfa — and those who hold his view — he divides this fifth into three categories, dropping from the division what belongs to the Messenger and what belongs to the near kin. His argument for this is that Abū Bakr and ʿUmar did not give the share of the near kin, and that the share of the Prophet ﷺ lapsed with his death, because the prophets are not inherited from. So it is divided among the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer according to the need of each group of them, and he may give some of them to the exclusion of others in particular, except that he does not take the division outside these three.
As for the school of Mālik, it is related that his view on this fifth and on the fayʾ is that these named ones are mentioned only because they are among the most important of those to whom payment is made. So he permits that it be divided among them, and permits giving some to the exclusion of others, and it is permissible to exclude them from the division if the affair of others is more pressing than theirs; he does this according to need. His argument for this is that the matter of alms has always been conducted in practice according to what people deem fit, and Allah — Mighty and Majestic — said: ﴿إنَّما الصَّدَقاتُ لِلْفُقَراءِ والمَساكِينِ والعامِلِينَ عَلَيْها والمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهم وفي الرِّقابِ والغارِمِينَ وفي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 60]; yet if five dirhams were due from a man, he would give them to one category of these, or to whichever of these categories he wished. Had the mention of the naming made the right obligatory for the whole group, it would not be permissible for one to be singled out to the exclusion of another, nor for one to be given less than what another is given.
Abū Isḥāq said: Among Mālik's arguments that the mention of these was only by way of particularising is His words — Exalted is He —: ﴿مَن كانَ عَدُوًّا لِلَّهِ ومَلائِكَتِهِ ورُسُلِهِ وجِبْرِيلَ ومِيكالَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 98]: He mentioned the angels as a whole, so Jibrīl and Mīkāl were already included in the whole, yet they were mentioned by their names to single them out. Likewise the mention of these in the division, the fayʾ and alms is because they are among the most important of those to whom wealth is directed in piety and alms.
Abū Isḥāq said: Also among the arguments for Mālik is the word of Allah — Mighty and Majestic —: ﴿يَسْألُونَكَ ماذا يُنْفِقُونَ قُلْ ما أنْفَقْتُمْ مِن خَيْرٍ فَلِلْوالِدَيْنِ والأقْرَبِينَ واليَتامى والمَساكِينِ وابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 215]: a man may spend in piety on these categories, or on one category of them, and he may go outside these categories; there is no disagreement among people about that. Abū Isḥāq said: This is the sum of what we know of the views of the jurists on this verse.
His words — Mighty and Majestic —: ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ آمَنتُمْ بِاللَّهِ وما أنْـزَلْنا عَلى عَبْدِنا﴾ — it is possible that "إنْ كُنْتُمْ" is connected to His words: ﴿فاعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلاكم نِعْمَ المَوْلى ونِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 40] ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ آمَنتُمْ بِاللَّهِ وما أنْـزَلْنا عَلى عَبْدِنا يَوْمَ الفُرْقانِ يَوْمَ التَقى الجَمْعانِ﴾ — so be certain that Allah has helped you, since you have witnessed of His help what you have witnessed. And it is possible that "إنْ كُنْتُمْ آمَنتُمْ بِاللَّهِ" means: know that whatever you take as spoils, its fifth belongs to Allah and to the Messenger, the two of them commanding regarding it what they will; if you have believed in Allah, then accept what you have been commanded regarding the spoils.
His words — Majestic and Mighty —: ﴿يَوْمَ الفُرْقانِ﴾ — it is the day of Badr, because on it Allah — Mighty and Majestic — manifested of His help, by sending the angels in succession and reinforcing the Muslims with them, that which was a criterion (furqān) between truth and falsehood.

zajjaj:42-42.t:
Then He reinforced the clarification of that, and said — Mighty and Majestic —: ﴿إذْ أنْتُمْ بِالعُدْوَةِ الدُّنْيا﴾, that is: the one nearer to you. "اَلْعُدْوَةُ" is the edge of the valley; one says "عِدْوَةٌ" and "عُدْوَةٌ", and "عِدى الوادِي" with a short final alif (maqṣūr). So the meaning is: "When you were at the nearer bank," that is: at the edge of the valley adjoining Medina, and they were at the farther bank, at the edge of the valley adjoining Mecca. ﴿والرَّكْبُ أسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾ — "اَلرَّكْبُ" is the caravan in which Abū Sufyān was, on the seashore. So Allah — Majestic and Mighty — made known that the victory of the believers while they were in this position was a furqān (criterion). Abū Isḥāq said: We have explained that it was sand in which the feet sank, and they were not at water, while the idolaters were encamped at a place where there was water, and in addition they were defending the caravan, which made their might all the greater. So Allah — Majestic and Mighty — made the victory in this situation, with the small number of the Muslims and the large number of the idolaters and the intensity of their might, a furqān.
In His words ﴿والرَّكْبُ أسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾ two ways are possible. The proper way is to make "أسْفَلَ" accusative, and the reading is upon that. It is also possible to make "أسْفَلُ" nominative, meaning "والرَّكْبُ أسْفَلُ مِنكم", that is: lower in position. Whoever reads the accusative intends: "والرَّكْبُ مَكانًا أسْفَلَ مِنكم" (the caravan was in a place lower than you).
His words: ﴿لِيَهْلِكَ مَن هَلَكَ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ ويَحْيا مَن حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ﴾ — Allah — Mighty and Majestic — made the one who aims at the truth like the living, and made the one who strays like the perishing. "حَيِيَ" with two yāʾs, and "حَيَّ" with a single doubled, assimilated yāʾ, are both permissible, and it has been read with both. As for al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, they both permit assimilation (idghām) and keeping the letters distinct (iẓhār) when the vowel on the second one is constant. Whoever assimilates does so because two letters of one kind have come together; whoever keeps them distinct does so because the second letter shifts away from the form of yāʾ: you say "حَيِيَ، يَحْيا" and "اَلْمَحْيا، والمَماتُ"; on this basis keeping them distinct is permissible. As for His words — Mighty and Majestic —: ﴿هُوَ يُحْيِي ويُمِيتُ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 158],
and His words: ﴿ألَيْسَ ذَلِكَ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أنْ يُحْيِيَ المَوْتى﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 40], according to all the Basrans nothing is permissible in it except "يُحْيِيَ" with two overt yāʾs. Some of them allowed "يُحَيِّ" with a single doubled, assimilated yāʾ, and it was mentioned that one of them recited:
وَكَأنَّها بَيْنَ النِّساءِ سَبِيكَةٌ ∗∗∗ تَمْشِي بِسُدَّةِ بَيْتِها فَتَعِي
(It is as though she, among the women, were an ingot of precious metal, walking at the threshold of her house and growing weary.)
If this reciter who cited it as evidence had informed us who this poet is, from which tribe he is, and whether he is one whose poetry is accepted as evidence or not, that would have done him no harm. It is not right that the Book of Allah should be interpreted on the basis of "someone recited to me," nor on the basis of an anomalous verse — even if its author were known and were one whose word is accepted, it would not be permissible. In our view this is permissible neither in prose nor in poetry, because when the second letter is vowelless in a sound (non-weak) verb, as in "لَمْ يَوَدَّ", the preferred choice is to show the doubling separately; so how much more so when it is from a weak verb.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
His words: ﴿إذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ في مَنامِكَ قَلِيلا﴾ — it is related from al-Ḥasan that its meaning is: "in your eye with which you sleep." Many grammarians adopt this view, and its meaning for them is: "When Allah showed them to you in the place of your sleeping," that is: with your eye; then the word "place" was omitted and the word for sleep was put in its stead. This is a good view; however, it has come in the exegesis that the Prophet ﷺ saw them in sleep as few and related the dream to his Companions, and they said: "Your dream has come true, O Messenger of Allah." This view is more acceptable in Arabic, because there has come: ﴿وَإذْ يُرِيكُمُوهم إذِ التَقَيْتُمْ في أعْيُنِكم قَلِيلا ويُقَلِّلُكم في أعْيُنِهِمْ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 44], so this indicates that this is the seeing at the encounter and that the other is the seeing in sleep. According to the first view, it is possible that the first address is to the Prophet ﷺ and that the second address is to all who witnessed the battle, and to the Prophet ﷺ.
His words: ﴿وَلَوْ أراكَهم كَثِيرًا لَفَشِلْتُمْ﴾, that is: you would have held back from fighting them, shrunk back, and been cowardly. One says: "فَشِلَ فَشَلًا" when someone becomes cowardly and is afraid to advance.

zajjaj:46-46.t: His words: ﴿وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: your assault and your strength will go. And one says regarding the first: "اَلرِّيحُ مَعَ فُلانٍ" (the wind is with so-and-so), that is: the ascendancy.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His words: ﴿وَإذْ زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ — the position of "إذْ" is accusative; the meaning is: "Remember when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them." ﴿وَقالَ لا غالِبَ لَكُمُ اليَوْمَ مِنَ النّاسِ وإنِّي جارٌ لَكُمْ﴾ — Iblīs appeared to them in the form of a man called Surāqa ibn Mālik ibn Juʿthum, of Kināna, and said to them: "No one will overcome you, and I am your protector from Banū Kināna." ﴿فَلَمّا تَراءَتِ الفِئَتانِ﴾ — they came face to face until each saw the other; Iblīs caught sight of the angels descending from the sky, so he turned back on his heels. ﴿وَقالَ إنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِنكُمْ﴾ — that was because he was reproached for his flight, so he said: "I am quit of you." ﴿إنِّي أرى ما لا تَرَوْنَ إنِّي أخافُ اللَّهَ واللَّهُ شَدِيدُ العِقابِ﴾. The meaning of "نَكَصَ" is: he went back in disgrace.
If someone says: How can Iblīs say "I fear Allah" when he is a disbeliever? The answer to that is that he thought the time until which he had been granted respite had arrived.

zajjaj:54-54.t: His words: ﴿كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ والَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ — its meaning is: the habit of these in their disbelief is like the habit of Pharaoh's people in their disbelief; so these were requited with killing and captivity, just as Pharaoh's people were requited with drowning and destruction. Thus some of the lexicographers said of "اَلدَّأْبُ": it is "habit". Abū Isḥāq said: The true sense of "اَلدَّأبُ" is persistence in work. You say: "فُلانٌ يَدْأبُ في كَذا وكَذا", that is: he persists in it, keeps at it diligently and wearies himself in it. This explanation is the meaning of "habit", except that it is clearer and more revealing.

zajjaj:55-55.t: His words: ﴿إنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — He meant that these will never believe, as He said to Nūḥ: ﴿أنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إلا مَن قَدْ آمَنَ﴾ [Hūd: 36].

zajjaj:57-57.t:
His words: ﴿فَإمّا تَثْقَفَنَّهم في الحَرْبِ فَشَرِّدْ بِهِمْ مَن خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: "Deal with them by such killing as will scatter those behind them."
His words — Mighty and Majestic —: ﴿تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: "you come upon them and meet them."

zajjaj:58-58.t: His words — Mighty and Majestic —: ﴿وَإمّا تَخافَنَّ مِن قَوْمٍ خِيانَةً﴾, that is: a breaking of the covenant. ﴿فانْبِذْ إلَيْهِمْ عَلى سَواءٍ﴾, that is: throw back their covenant which you made with them — that is, cast it away. ﴿عَلى سَواءٍ﴾, that is: so that you and they are equal in enmity. ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الخائِنِينَ﴾, that is: those who are treacherous in their covenant and otherwise.

zajjaj:59-59.t:
His words: ﴿وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَبَقُوا إنَّهم لا يُعْجِزُونَ﴾ — its meaning is: "Let not whoever escaped from this battle think that he has escaped ahead to life." The good reading is "وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ" with tāʾ, as an address to the Prophet ﷺ; "تَحْسَبَنَّ" then governs "اَلَّذِينَ", and "سَبَقُوا" is the khabar (predicate). The sīn may be read with fatḥa or with kasra. Some of the readers read "وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا" with yāʾ; its justification is weak in the view of the experts in Arabic, though it is permissible, on the basis that the meaning is: "Let not those who disbelieved think that they have outstripped," because in the codex (ḥarf) of Ibn Masʿūd it is "إنَّهم سَبَقُوا". If it is so, it is like your saying "حَسِبْتُ أنْ أقُومَ" and "حَسِبْتُ أقُومُ" with "أنْ" omitted, and "أقُومُ" and "قامَ" stand in for the noun and the predicate, just as when you say "ظَنَنْتُ لَزَيْدٌ خَيْرٌ مِنكَ" (I thought: Zayd is surely better than you), the clause stands in for the noun and predicate of ظَنّ (thinking). There is another way in it: "Let not the party of the believers think that those who disbelieved have outstripped."
Several ways are possible in it that have not been read: "وَلا يُحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَبَقُوا" is possible, and "﴿وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾" «[Translator's note: the text as transmitted repeats the Quranic wording here; the variant intended is apparently a different construal or vocalisation, as the gloss that follows shows.]», that is: "Let not the believers think that those who disbelieved have outstripped"; but reading is a sunna (established practice), and one reads only as the readers have read. "إنَّهم" with kasra on "إنَّ" is possible, and "أنَّهم" is possible, so that the meaning is: "Let not those who disbelieved think that they can frustrate," with "أنَّ" being a badal (substitute) for "سَبَقُوا". Abū Isḥāq said: This way is weak, because "لا" is not redundant (laghw) in a position where it can occur as non-redundant.
His words: "يُعْجِزُونَ" — fatḥa on the nūn is the preferred choice, and kasra on it is possible, with the meaning being "إنَّهم لا يُعْجِزُونَنِي" (they cannot frustrate Me), the first nūn being omitted because of the meeting of the two nūns. The poet said:
رَأتْهُ كالنَّعامِ يُعَلُّ مِسْكًا ∗∗∗ يَسُوءُ الفالِياتِ إذا فَلَيْنِي
(She saw it like the ostriches, scented again and again with musk; it vexes the women who search it for lice when they search me.)
He means: "فَلَيْنَنِي".

zajjaj:60-60.t: His words: ﴿وَآخَرِينَ مِن دُونِهِمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَهُمُ اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُهُمْ﴾ — "وَآخَرِينَ" is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to His words ﴿تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِ عَدُوَّ اللَّهِ وعَدُوَّكُمْ﴾, that is: and you strike terror into others besides them.

zajjaj:61-61.t: His words: ﴿وَإنْ جَنَحُوا لِلسَّلْمِ فاجْنَحْ لَها﴾ — "اَلسَّلْمُ" is reconciliation and making peace. One says "سِلْمٌ", "سَلْمٌ" and "سَلَمٌ" with one meaning; that is: "If they incline to reconciliation, then incline to it."

zajjaj:62-62.t: ﴿وَإنْ يُرِيدُوا أنْ يَخْدَعُوكَ﴾, that is: if by making a show of reconciliation they intend to deceive you, ﴿فَإنَّ حَسْبَكَ اللَّهُ﴾, that is: the One who undertakes to suffice you is Allah. ﴿وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 64] — the position of "مَن" is accusative or nominative. Whoever takes it as accusative does so according to the interpretation of the kāf; the meaning is: "Allah suffices you and suffices those of the believers who follow you." Whoever takes it as nominative does so by conjoining it to "اللَّهُ", and the meaning is: "Your sufficiency is Allah and your followers among the believers." ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أيَّدَكَ بِنَصْرِهِ وبِالمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — the meaning of "أيَّدَكَ" is: He strengthened you.

zajjaj:63-63.t:
﴿وَبِالمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 62] ﴿وَألَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, that is: He gathered them in affection upon faith.
His words: ﴿لَوْ أنْفَقْتَ ما في الأرْضِ جَمِيعًا﴾ — "جَمِيعًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ما ألَّفْتَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ ألَّفَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ — Allah — Majestic and Mighty — made known that the uniting of the believers' hearts is among the great signs. That is because the Prophet ﷺ was sent to a people whose pride was fierce, and whose help and support for one another was the most far-reaching help and support: if a man of the tribe received a single slap, they would fight on his behalf until his vengeance was obtained. Then faith united their hearts, so that a man would fight his father, his brother and his son. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic — made known that none but He brought this about among them.

zajjaj:65-65.t:
His words: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ حَرِّضِ المُؤْمِنِينَ عَلى القِتالِ﴾ — its interpretation is: "Urge them on to fighting." The interpretation of "اَلتَّحْرِيضُ" in the language is that a person is urged to something with such urging that it is understood with it that he is "حارِضٌ" if he holds back from it; and "اَلْحارِضُ" is one who has come close to perishing. His words — Exalted is He —: ﴿حَتّى تَكُونَ حَرَضًا﴾ [Yūsuf: 85], that is: until you waste away with grief, come close to perishing, and become one of those who perish.
His words: ﴿إنْ يَكُنْ مِنكم عِشْرُونَ صابِرُونَ﴾ — nothing but kasra on the ʿayn is permissible. The lexicographers claimed that the first letter of "عِشْرِينَ" was given kasra just as the first letter of "اِثْنَيْنِ" was, because "عِشْرِينَ" is from "عَشَرَةٌ" as "اِثْنَيْنِ" is from "واحِدٌ". Their evidence for this is that they give fatḥa to "ثَلاثِينَ" like the fatḥa of "ثَلاثَةٌ", and the kasra of "تِسْعِينَ" is like the kasra of "تِسْعَةٌ".

zajjaj:66-66.t: His words: ﴿وَعَلِمَ أنَّ فِيكم ضَعْفًا﴾ — it has been read in three ways. It has been read "ضَعْفًا" with fatḥa on the ḍād and "ضُعْفًا" with ḍamma on the ḍād, and the meaning is the same; one says "هو الضَّعْفُ، والضُّعْفُ", "اَلْمَكْثُ، والمُكْثُ" and "اَلْفَقْرُ، والفُقْرُ"; the pattern of "فَعْلٌ" and "فُعْلٌ" with one meaning is common in the language. And one of the elders read "وَعَلِمَ أنَّ فِيكم ضُعَفاءَ" on the pattern "فُعَلاءَ", as the plural of "ضَعِيفٌ" — "ضُعَفاءُ" — and it is not declined as a triptote and takes no tanwīn, because "فُعَلاءَ" has the feminine alif at its end. ﴿فَإنْ يَكُنْ مِنكم مِائَةٌ صابِرَةٌ﴾ — it has also been read "فَإنْ تَكُنْ" with tāʾ. Whoever makes it feminine does so because the word "مِائَةٌ" is feminine in form; whoever makes it masculine does so because "مِائَةٌ" refers to a number, so it is made masculine.

zajjaj:67-67.t: His words: ﴿ما كانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ أسْرى﴾ — it is also read "أُسارى". Whoever reads "أسْرى", it is the plural of "أسِيرٌ": "أسْرى". "فَعْلى" is a plural for all those who have been afflicted in their bodies and minds; one says "هالِكُ / هَلْكى" (perishing), "مَرِيضُ / مَرْضى" (sick), "أحْمَقُ / حَمْقى" (foolish), and "سَكْرانُ / سَكْرى" (drunk). Whoever reads "أُسارى", it is a plural of the plural; you say "أسِيرٌ" and "أُسارى". Abū Isḥāq said: I know of no one who read it "أسارى" «[Translator's note: presumably أَسارى with fatḥa, as distinct from أُسارى above; the printed text does not mark the vowel.]», and it is permissible, but do not read it so unless a sound transmission is established. ﴿حَتّى يُثْخِنَ في الأرْضِ﴾ — its meaning is: until he has gone to great lengths in killing his enemies; and it may mean "until he is firmly established in the land." "اَلْإثْخانُ" in everything is the strength of the thing and its severity; one says: "قَدْ أثْخَنْتُهُ" (I have weakened him severely).

zajjaj:75-75.t: The meaning of ﴿وَأُولُو الأرْحامِ بَعْضُهم أوْلى بِبَعْضٍ﴾ is: some of them have a prior claim on others in inheritance. These inheritances through the bond of hijra (emigration) are abrogated; they were abrogated by the obligatory shares in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Anfāl
﷽
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَسْألُونَكَ عَنِ الأنْفالِ قُلِ الأنْفالُ لِلَّهِ والرَّسُولِ﴾: "اَلْأنْفالُ" are the spoils of war; its singular is "نَفَلٌ". Labīd said:
؎إنَّ تَقْوى رَبِّنا خَيْرُ نَفَلْ ∗∗∗ وبِإذْنِ اللَّهِ رَيْثِي وعَجَلْ
(Truly, fear of our Lord is the best of gains, and by Allah's leave are my tarrying and my haste.)
They asked about them only because, according to what has been related, they had been forbidden to those before them. It is related that the people in the expedition of "Badr" were few, so the Prophet ﷺ assigned to whoever brought a captive a share of booty, and to whoever brought two captives in proportion to that. It was also said that he granted extra shares (nafal) in the raiding parties. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿الأنْفالُ لِلَّهِ والرَّسُولِ﴾ (the spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger).

zajjaj:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّما المُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ إذا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾: its interpretation is: "When the greatness of Allah, His power, and what He has threatened those who disobey Him with are mentioned, their hearts tremble", that is: "they are alarmed at that". The poet said:
؎لَعَمْرُكَ ما أدْرِي وإنِّي لِأوْجَلُ ∗∗∗ عَلى أيِّنا تَعْدُو المَنِيَّةُ أوَّلُ
(By your life, I do not know, and indeed I am afraid, upon which of us death will first fall.)
One says "وَجِلَ، يَوْجَلُ، وجَلًا", and in the sense of "يَوْجَلُ" one says "ياجَلُ، يِيجَلُ، ويَيْجَلُ". These are four dialectal forms which Sībawayh reported, and the best of them is "يَوْجَلُ"; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿لا تَوْجَلْ إنّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 53].
His saying: ﴿وَإذا تُلِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُهُ زادَتْهم إيمانًا﴾: the interpretation of "اَلْإيمانُ" is affirmation of truth (taṣdīq); whatever was recited to them from Allah they affirmed as true, so their affirming that increased their faith.
His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ المُؤْمِنُونَ حَقًّا﴾ [al-Anfāl: 4]: "حَقًّا" is accusative by a meaning indicated by the sentence, and the sentence is "أُولَئِكَ هُمُ المُؤْمِنُونَ"; so the meaning is: "I affirm that truly (أحُقُّ ذَلِكَ حَقًّا)".
His saying: ﴿لَهم دَرَجاتٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 4] means: they have ranks in elevation according to their stations.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿كَما أخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَيْتِكَ بِالحَقِّ﴾ means: with the binding truth. Its interpretation would be: ﴿كَما أخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَيْتِكَ بِالحَقِّ وإنَّ فَرِيقًا مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ لَكارِهُونَ﴾, "likewise We grant extra spoils to whomever We see fit, even if they dislike it"; because one of the Companions said to the Prophet ﷺ, when he assigned something to everyone who brought a captive: "Most of the people will be left with nothing".
So the position of the kāf in "كَما" is accusative; the meaning is: "The spoils are established for you, just like your Lord's bringing you out of your house with the truth".
His saying: ﴿فاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وأصْلِحُوا ذاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 1]: the meaning of "ذاتَ بَيْنِكم" is the reality of your bond; "اَلْبَيْنُ" is the bond (connection). The Exalted said: ﴿لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 94], that is: your bond. So the meaning is: "Fear Allah and be united upon what Allah and His Messenger have commanded". Likewise "اَللَّهُمَّ أصْلِحْ ذاتَ البَيْنِ", that is: "O Allah, set right the state by which the Muslims are united".
His saying: ﴿وَأطِيعُوا اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 1] means: accept what you have been commanded concerning the spoils and other matters.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿يُجادِلُونَكَ في الحَقِّ بَعْدَما تَبَيَّنَ﴾: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, promised them in the expedition of "Badr" that they would gain victory over the people of Mecca and over the caravan (al-ʿīr), that is, the camels; and because of their dislike of fighting they disputed with the Prophet ﷺ and said: "We only set out for the caravan".
[Translator's note: the text has "and over the caravan" (وبِالعِيرِ); the promise in the verse is of one of the two parties (cf. 8:7), so "or over the caravan" may be intended.]
His saying: ﴿كَأنَّما يُساقُونَ إلى المَوْتِ﴾ means: in going out to fight they were as though being driven to death, because of their small number and because they were on foot; it is related that there were only two horsemen among them, so they were afraid.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذْ يَعِدُكُمُ اللَّهُ إحْدى الطّائِفَتَيْنِ أنَّها لَكُمْ﴾: the meaning is: "And remember when Allah promised you that one of the two parties would be yours".
﴿أنَّها لَكُمْ﴾ is in the position of the accusative, as a badal (substitute) for "إحْدى". Similar to it is His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلا رِجالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ ونِساءٌ مُؤْمِناتٌ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهم أنْ تَطَئُوهُمْ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 25]; the meaning is: "And were it not that you would trample them".
His saying: ﴿وَتَوَدُّونَ أنَّ غَيْرَ ذاتِ الشَّوْكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمْ﴾ means: you wished that the party in which there was no fighting and no weapons, namely the camels, would be yours. "ذاتُ الشَّوْكَةِ" is the one with weapons. One says "فُلانٌ شاكٍ في السِّلاحِ", "شائِكٌ في السِّلاحِ", and "شاكٌّ في السِّلاحِ" with the kāf doubled, from "اَلشِّكَةُ" (armour). An example of "شاكِي" is the poet's saying:
؎فَتَعَرَّفُونِي إنَّنِي أنا ذاكُمُ ∗∗∗ شاكٍ سِلاحِي في الحَوادِثِ مُعْلِمُ
(So recognise me: I am that man, sharp-weaponed in calamities, wearing the mark of a champion.)
His saying: ﴿وَيُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أنْ يُحِقَّ الحَقَّ بِكَلِماتِهِ ويَقْطَعَ دابِرَ الكافِرِينَ﴾ means: "Your victory over the armed party cuts off their root more completely".

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿إذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكم فاسْتَجابَ لَكُمْ﴾: when they saw how few they were in number, they sought help, so Allah reinforced them with the angels. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أنِّي مُمِدُّكم بِألْفٍ مِنَ المَلائِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ﴾.
One says "رَدِفْتُ الرَّجُلَ" when I rode behind him, and "أرْدَفُتُهُ" when I made him ride behind me. One says "هَذِهِ دابَّةٌ لا تُرادِفُ" (this is a mount that does not carry a second rider), but one does not say "لا تُرْدَفُ". And one says "أرْدَفْتُ الرَّجُلَ" when I came after him. So the meaning of "مُرْدِفِينَ" is: coming group after group.
It is also read "مُرْدَفِينَ"; and in the language "مَرَدَّفِينَ" is permissible, as are "مُرِدِّفِينَ" and "مُرَدَّفِينَ": with the dāl doubled, the rāʾ may take kasra, fatḥa or ḍamma, and the dāl is doubled with kasra in every case. Sībawayh said: the origin is "مُرْتَدِفِينَ"; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl and it became "مُرَدِّفِينَ", because you cast the vowel of the tāʾ onto the rāʾ. He said: and if you wish, you do not cast the vowel of the tāʾ, and you give the rāʾ kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. Those who gave the rāʾ ḍamma made it follow the ḍamma of the mīm.
[Translator's note: the forms are given as vowelled in the text; e.g. "مَرَدَّفِينَ" and "مُرَدَّفِينَ" appear with fatḥa on the dāl, although the text then says the dāl has kasra in every case.]

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَما جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إلا بُشْرى﴾ means: Allah made the reinforcement only as good tidings.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿إذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ النُّعاسَ﴾: the position of "إذْ" is accusative, in the sense of "and Allah made it only good tidings at that time"; and it may be on the basis of: "Remember when He covered you with drowsiness". One says "نَعَسَ الرَّجُلُ يَنْعَسُ نُعاسًا، وهو ناعِسٌ" (the man dozed, he dozes, dozing, and he is drowsy); some say "نَعْسانُ", but I do not like it.
And "أمَنَةً" is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), like your saying: "I did that out of caution against evil". The interpretation is that Allah gave them such security that drowsiness overcame them, because of the victory He had promised them. One says: "قَدْ آمَنتُ، آمَنُ، أمْنًا (with fatḥa on the alif), وأمانًا، وأمَنَةً".
His saying: ﴿وَيُنَـزِّلُ عَلَيْكم مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً لِيُطَهِّرَكم بِهِ﴾: the polytheists had encamped at the water, having got there before the Muslims, and the Muslims encamped on sand in which the feet sank; and some of them were in a state of major ritual impurity (janāba). Satan whispered to them that their enemy had access to the water while they had no access to the water, and it was made to appear to them that this was help from Allah for their enemy. So Allah sent rain on the place where they were, and they purified themselves with the water, and the ground they were on became firm, so that it was possible to stand on it and move about. This is among the signs of Allah, exalted be His praise, which indicate the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ. The affair of "Badr" was among the greatest of signs, because the number of the Muslims was very small and they were on foot, yet Allah strengthened them; the polytheists were many times their number, and Allah reinforced them with the angels. Some said the angels were five thousand, and some said nine thousand.
His saying: ﴿وَيُذْهِبَ عَنْكم رِجْزَ الشَّيْطانِ﴾ means: his whisperings and his evil suggestions. "And to make firm the feet thereby", that is: "and to make firm (the feet) by the water which He sent down on the sand until it became level". It is also possible that He made (the rain) a means of strengthening their hearts, so that the meaning would be: "And to strengthen your hearts and make firm the feet by the strengthening".
[Translator's note: "زَيَّنَ بِهِ لِلرَّبْطِ" (He adorned with it for the strengthening) is as in the text; it is rendered by its evident sense.]

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ﴾: "إذْ" is in the position of the accusative on the basis of "and to strengthen ... when He revealed"; and it may be on the basis of "Remember". "So make firm those who believe": it is possible that they (the angels) made them firm by things they cast into their hearts by which they grew strong; and it is possible that they saw them as reinforcements, and when they beheld the angels' help, they stood firm.
His saying: ﴿فاضْرِبُوا فَوْقَ الأعْناقِ واضْرِبُوا مِنهم كُلَّ بَنانٍ﴾: Allah permitted them to kill them by every means in war. The singular of "اَلْبَنانُ" is "بَنانَةٌ", and its meaning here is the fingers and the other limbs, all of them. The derivation of "اَلْبَنانُ" is from their saying "أبَنَّ بِالمَكانِ" when he stayed in the place; so the bunān is that with which one works everything that serves residence and life.
[Translator's note: the last clause reads "فالبِناءُ بِهِ يَعْتَمِلُ كُلَّ ما يَكُونُ لِلْإقامَةِ والحَياةِ" in the text; "البِناء" is probably a corruption of "البَنان", and it is translated in that sense.]

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهم شاقُّوا اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ﴾: "شاقُّوا" means: they took a side apart; they placed themselves on a side (shiqq) other than the side of the believers. Like "شاقُّوا" are "جانَبُوا", "حازَبُوا" and "حارَبُوا"; the meaning of "حازَبُوا" is: these became a party and those became a party.
﴿وَمَن يُشاقِقِ اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ العِقابِ﴾: "يُشاقِقْ" and "يُشاقِّ" are both (correct), except that here it is "يُشاقِقْ", with the doubling shown openly in the jussive, which is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz; others assimilate. When you assimilate, you say "مَن يُشاقَّ زَيْدًا أُهِنْهُ" (whoever opposes Zayd, I will humiliate him), with fatḥa on the qāf, because the two qāfs are vowelless, so the second was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and because there is an alif before it. If you wish, you give it kasra and say "يُشاقِّ زَيْدًا", with kasra on the qāf, because the basic vowel for the meeting of two vowelless letters is kasra. When the alif and lām (the definite article) come after it, you choose the kasra and say "وَمَن يُشاقِّ اللَّهَ"; but I do not know anyone who read it so.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿إذا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا زَحْفًا﴾: one says "أزَحَفْتُ لِلْقَوْمِ" when I stood firm against them. So the meaning is: "When you face them in battle, ﴿فَلا تُوَلُّوهُمُ الأدْبارَ﴾", that is: "do not be routed so that you turn your backs".
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُ إلا مُتَحَرِّفًا﴾ [al-Anfāl: 16] means the day of their battle. ﴿إلا مُتَحَرِّفًا﴾ [al-Anfāl: 16] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The accusative in "مُتَحَرِّفًا" and "مُتَحَيِّزًا" may also be by way of exception (istithnāʾ), that is: "except a man withdrawing (to a group)", that is: he is isolated, so he withdraws in order to be with the fighters. The origin of "مُتَحَيِّزٌ" is "مُتَحَيْوِزٌ", and the yāʾ was assimilated into the wāw.
[Translator's note: so in the text; in the usual description the wāw is changed to yāʾ and assimilated into the yāʾ.]

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهم ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ﴾ is also read "وَلَكِنِ اللَّهُ قَتَلَهم". Whoever doubles (the nūn) puts (the name) in the accusative because "لَكِنَّ" governs the accusative; whoever lightens it cancels its government and makes His saying "اَللَّهُ" nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Allah attributed killing them to Himself because He is the One who took charge of their (the believers') victory and displayed miraculous signs in that.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما رَمَيْتَ إذْ رَمَيْتَ﴾: this is not a negation of the Prophet's ﷺ throwing; rather, the Arabs were addressed in terms they understand. It is related «that the Prophet ﷺ said to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq: "Hand me a handful of pebbles from the river bed", so he handed him a handful and he threw it, and not one of them, I mean of the enemy, remained but was preoccupied with his eye». So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that a handful of earth or pebbles does not fill the eyes of that great army by the throw of a human being, and that He, Mighty and Majestic, took charge of conveying it to their eyes. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَما رَمَيْتَ إذْ رَمَيْتَ﴾, that is: that throw of yours did not hit, nor reach that extent through you; it was Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who took charge of that. This is the figurative sense (majāz) of "﴿وَما رَمَيْتَ إذْ رَمَيْتَ ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمى﴾".
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلِيُبْلِيَ المُؤْمِنِينَ مِنهُ بَلاءً حَسَنًا﴾ means: to help them with a fine victory and to test them with what is best. The meaning of "يُبْلِيَهم" here is: to bestow (favour) upon them.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: "﴿ذَلِكم وأنَّ اللَّهَ مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ الكافِرِينَ﴾", (read also) with the hāʾ doubled (مُوَهِّنٌ) and with the accusative in "كَيْدَ"; the genitive in "كَيْدِ" is also permissible, with "مُوهِنُ" annexed to it. So there are four ways in it: two ways in the accusative and two ways in the genitive. The position of "ذَلِكم" is nominative; the meaning is: "The matter is that, and that Allah…", and "the matter is that Allah weakens…".
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكم فَذُوقُوهُ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 14]: the position of "ذَلِكم" is nominative with "اَلْأمْرُ" (the matter) implied; the meaning is: "The matter is that, so taste it". Whoever says that "ذَلِكم" is made nominative by the hāʾ that refers back to it, or as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and makes the khabar (predicate) "فَذُوقُوهُ", has erred, because what comes after the fāʾ cannot be the predicate of a subject: "زَيْدٌ فَمُنْطَلِقٌ" is not permissible, nor "زَيْدٌ فاضْرِبْهُ", unless you imply "هَذا" (this), meaning "هَذا زَيْدٌ فاضْرِبْهُ" (this is Zayd, so strike him). The poet said:
؎وَقائِلَةٍ خَوْلانُ فانْكِحْ فَتاتَهم ∗∗∗ وأُكْرُومَةُ الحَيَّيْنِ خِلْوٌ كَما هِيا
(And many a woman saying: "(These are) Khawlān, so marry their maiden" — while the noblest girl of the two clans is still unwed, as she was.)
Someone mentioned that it (أنَّ لِلْكافِرِينَ) could be in the position of the accusative with "واعْلَمُوا أنَّ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابَ النّارِ" (and know that for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire) implied. It would follow from this that one could say "زَيْدٌ مُنْطَلِقٌ وعَمْرًا قائِمًا" in the sense of "and know Amr to be standing"; indeed it would follow that he could say "عَمْرًا مُنْطَلِقًا", because whoever gives information is making known. But implying "اِعْلَمْ" is not permissible here, because in every statement by which information is given or sought you are making something known, so there is no need to express "knowing" overtly or to imply it. And this view has not been held by any of the grammarians.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿إنْ تَسْتَفْتِحُوا فَقَدْ جاءَكُمُ الفَتْحُ﴾ means: "If you seek victory, victory has come to you". It may also mean: "If you seek judgement, judgement has come to you". The exegesis has come with both meanings. They related that Abū Jahl said on the day of "Badr": "O Allah, whichever of us is more given to cutting the ties of kinship and more corrupting to the community, destroy him today". So he asked Allah to decree destruction for whoever was like that; then the Prophet ﷺ was given victory, and destruction befell Abū Jahl and his companions. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إنْ تَسْتَفْتِحُوا فَقَدْ جاءَكُمُ الفَتْحُ﴾, that is: "If you seek a decision, the decision has come to you". It was also said that he said: "O Allah, give victory to the dearer of the two parties to You"; this indicates that its meaning is "If you seek victory". Both aspects are good.
